X23C: Akal Purakh is One, and is found through the grace of the True Guru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but One God. By the True Guru's grace, is He obtained.
35QU: Raag Kanara, Ghar 1: a Bani of eight-stanza hymns by Guru Ram Das ji.
Kaanraa, Ashtpadheeyaa, Fourth Mehl, First House:
BQ3K: Jap = keep chanting. Man = O mind! Pavaigo = gains.
O (my) mind! Keep chanting (Parmatma's) Name (always); (the one who chants) finds peace.
Chant the Name of the Lord, O mind, and find peace.
O my soul, utter you the Lord's Name and you shall be blessed with peace.
O my mind! Chant Ram's Name; you will find peace.
AZ5U: Japai = chants. Sev = serving, taking shelter. Samavaigo = stays merged. ||1|| Rahau ||
The more (a person) chants (Hari's Name), the more bliss they enjoy, and taking the Guru's shelter they stay merged (in Hari's Name). ||1|| Rahau ||
The more you chant and meditate, the more you will be at peace; serve the True Guru, and merge in the Lord. ||1||Pause||
The more you remember God, the more peace you shall obtain. Serving the True Guru, you shall merge in the Lord. Pause.
The more you chant the Name, the more peace you will find, and serving the True Guru you will merge into Parmeshar. ||1|| Rahau ||
Z2BL: Khin khin = at every moment. Locha = longing. Japat = while chanting.
O mind! The devotees always long (to chant the Name); (Parmatma's devotee) finds bliss while chanting Hari's Name.
Each and every instant, the humble devotees long for Him; chanting the Naam, they find peace.
Every moment, the saintly persons long for the Name and, meditating on the Name, they obtain bliss.
In the understanding of the devotees there is, at every instant, the longing to chant the Name; you too will find peace by chanting the Name.
2WV8: An ras saad = the tastes of other pleasures. Neekar gae = went out, went away. ||1||
The tastes of all other pleasures go out (from within them); nothing but Hari's Name pleases (the devotee). ||1||
The taste of other pleasures is totally eradicated; nothing pleases them, except the Name. ||1||
Their relish of other pleasures is all eliminated and, save the Name, nothing pleases them.
When the tastes of (an ras) other pleasures have left your understanding, then nothing but the Name will feel good to you. ||1||
FBLF: Gur kadhavaigo = the Guru draws out.
O mind! Through the blessing of the Guru's teaching, Parmatma's Name begins to feel dear (to the devotee); the Guru draws out (from their mouth only) sweet words (of praise).
Following the Guru's Teachings, the Lord seems sweet to them; the Guru inspires them to speak sweet words.
By the Guru's instruction, the Lord God seems sweet to them and the Guru makes them utter sweet words.
When the Guru draws sweet words out of you — that is, makes you speak them — then, through His teaching, the Name Har Har will stay sweet to you.
Y8ZM: Purkhotam = the most exalted Being (Akal Purakh). Siu = with. Lavaigo = attaches. ||2||
Through the Guru's Bani (the devotee meets) Parmatma, the exalted Being; (so the devotee's) mind always melts with the Guru's Bani. ||2||
Through the Word of the True Guru's Bani, the Primal Lord God is revealed; so focus your consciousness on His Bani. ||2||
Through the True Guru's word, the sublime person is revealed and they fix their mind with the Guru's word.
The True Guru's Bani brings one to the supreme Being; when you fix your mind in that Bani, then you will find Him. ||2||
U6CK: Dravia = has softened. Bheena = has been soaked. Nij ghar = in one's own (true) home.
My mind is soaked (in the nectar of the Name); (instead of wandering outside) it stays settled in its true self.
Hearing the Word of the Guru's Bani, my mind has been softened and saturated with it; my mind has returned to its own home deep within.
Hearing the Guru's word, my mind has become tender and imbued with it, this mind has returned to its own home.
Hearing the Guru's Bani, my mind has melted. O beloved! You too, soaked in the love of Vahiguru, will come to your own home, the true self.
79A0: Tah = in that (heart-home). Anhat = unbroken, continuous. Dhuni = note. Bajah = keep playing. Neejhar = {nirjhara} spring. Chuavaigo = keeps trickling, keeps flowing. ||3||
Such bliss stays in the heart (as if) instruments keep playing there with an unbroken note, (as if) a stream (of water) from a spring keeps flowing. ||3||
The Unstruck Melody resonates and resounds there continuously; the stream of nectar trickles down constantly. ||3||
There resounds and ever resounds the celestial strain and the stream of Nectar incessantly trickles.
When there is the true company, (tah) there instruments of unbroken sound play always. There the (neejhar) unbroken stream of the bliss of the self will trickle for you. ||3||
68PB: Til til = at every moment. Gavai = keeps singing. Naam = in the Name.
O mind! (Parmatma's devotee) keeps chanting Parmatma's Name at every moment, with every breath; taking the Guru's teaching, (the devotee's) mind stays (always) merged in the Name.
Singing the Name of the One Lord each and every instant, and following the Guru's Teachings, the mind is absorbed in the Naam.
When man sings the praise of the Lord's Name at every moment, he then merges in the Name through the Guru's instruction.
Those saints sing Ram's Name at every (til til) instant; and there, through the Guru's teaching, your mind will merge into the Named One.
77VG: Naamo = the Name alone. Man = in the mind. Bhavai = feels dear. Naame = in the Name alone. Tripatavaigo = stays satisfied. ||4||
The devotee hears (Parmatma's) Name (at every moment); the Name alone feels dear in (their) mind; through the Name alone (the devotee) stays satisfied (free of craving for Maya). ||4||
Listening to the Naam, the mind is pleased with the Naam, and satisfied with the Naam. ||4||
God's Name he hears, God's Name pleases his mind and with God's Name, he is satiated.
You will hear the Name, and the Name alone will please your mind, and through the Name alone you will be satisfied. ||4||
NSEK: Kanik = gold. Kapar = cloth. Bhaant = of many kinds. Banavaigo = makes.
(O my mind! A person wrapped in Maya) wears many bangles (and other ornaments) of gold (and other precious metals); (to adorn their body) they have cloth of many kinds made,
People wear lots of bracelets, glittering with gold; they wear all sorts of fine clothes.
Thought man may don many bracelets of glittering gold and wear various sorts of clothes,
If you wear many ornaments, bangles and the like, of the finest of golds, and have clothes of many kinds made,
UXVS: Sabh = all. Pheek phikane = utterly tasteless. Janam = being born. ||5||
without (Parmatma's) Name all (these efforts) are utterly tasteless. (Such a person always) stays in the round of birth and death. ||5||
But without the Naam, they are all bland and insipid. They are born, only to die again, in the cycle of reincarnation. ||5||
but without the Lord's Name, they are all insipid and vain and he shall continue the cycle of birth and death.

then without the Name those ornaments are all tasteless, and the clothes and the rest are (phikane) without savour. If you fix your mind on these, you will come into the round of birth and death. ||5||
6V5F: Patal = veil. Ghooman gher = whirlpool. Ghulavaigo = struggles, suffers.

O my mind! The veil (of attachment to) Maya is a very heavy veil; (because of this veil of attachment, a person's) home becomes a whirlpool; (all their life the person) struggles (to keep from drowning in it).
The veil of Maya is a thick and heavy veil, a whirlpool which destroys one's home.
Mammon veil is a great veil and through it, man lands in the whirlpool of desire, in which his home is destroyed.
Of all (patal) veils, the veil of Maya is the heaviest; through it the (ghar) heart will be (ghulavaigo) mixed into the whirlpool of the senses.
GVD8: Manoor = burnt iron, slag. Bikh = poison (that brings spiritual death). Dutar = hard to cross. ||6||

The sins and vices (done while caught in attachment) become heavy (burdens) like slag; (because of them) it becomes hard to cross the poisonous (world-ocean) that brings spiritual death; (the one wrapped in Maya) cannot cross it. ||6||
Sins and corrupt vices are totally heavy, like rusted slag. They will not let you cross over the poisonous and treacherous world-ocean. ||6||
All the sins and vices are heavy like the rusted iron and with them the poisonous and arduous world ocean can be crossed not.
The being has taken up sins and vices on their head, heavy as slag; so the hard, poisonous world-ocean will not be crossed. ||6|| ☬ If you ask whether anyone will cross at all, he says:
6UZ9: Bhau = fear, reverence. Bairag = love, longing. Bohith = ship. Khevat = boatman. Sabad = through the Word. Taravaigo = carries across.

O my mind! Reverence and love (for Parmatma in the heart) become the ship (to cross the world-ocean); (the one within whom there is love and awe,) the Guru, the boatman, carries across through (His) Word.
Let the Fear of God and neutral detachment be the boat; the Guru is the Boatman, who carries us across in the Word of the Shabad.
God's fear and love are the ship and the Guru the helmsman, who ferries man across with the help of Lord's Name.
Those who, through fear and detachment, have gained the ship of knowledge, or of the Name — the Guru, the (khevat) boatman, will carry them across the world-ocean by His (sabad) teaching.
9LJD: Bheteeai = can be met. Ramai naam = in Parmatma's Name. ||7||
(Chanting) Parmatma's Name, Parmatma can be met; (the person within whom there is awe and love) stays merged in Prabhu's Name always. ||7||
Meeting with the Lord, the Name of the Lord, merge in the Lord, the Name of the Lord. ||7||
Meeting with the Lord God's Name, one merges in the Name of the Lord God.
When Hari's Name, Ram, is met, then the being will merge into Hari, the all-pervading Named One. ||7||
1MLQ: Agian = in ignorance. Lai = attaching. Gur giaanai = in the knowledge the Guru gives.

(Parmatma sometimes) catches a being in ignorance and keeps them asleep (in the sleep of attachment to Maya); sometimes He settles them in the spiritual understanding the Guru gives and wakes them (from that sleep).
Attached to ignorance, people are falling asleep; attached to the Guru's spiritual wisdom, they awaken.
Attached to ignorance, man is lulled to sleep and, yoking him to gnosis, the Guru awakens him.
Parmeshvar has attached beings to ignorance and put them to sleep; and through the Guru He will attach them to knowledge and wake them.
4R94: Bhanai = in the will. Bhavai = pleases. ||8||1||
O Nanak! As is Parmatma's will, so He leads (the being on the path of life). ||8||1||
O Nanak, by His Will, He makes us walk as He pleases. ||8||1||
O Nanak, in His will, the Lord makes man walk, in the same way as it pleases Him.
Sri Guru ji says: in His own will, as it pleases Him, so He leads beings in all three times. ||8||1||
WCH8: Jap = keep chanting. Man = O mind! Taravaigo = carries across.
O (my) mind! Keep chanting Parmatma's Name; Hari's Name carries (a person) across (the world-ocean).
O mind, chant the Name of the Lord, Har, Har, and be carried across.
O my soul, utter you the Lord God's Name and it shall ferry you across.
O mind! Chant the Name Har Har; it will carry you across the world-ocean.
NG54: Jo jo = whoever. Soee = that one alone. Gat = high spiritual state. Samavaigo = has kept merging. ||1|| Rahau ||
Whoever chants Hari's Name reaches the high spiritual state (and merges into Parmatma), just as Dhru and Prahlad merged (into Prabhu, each in his own time). ||1|| Rahau ||
Whoever chants and meditates on it is emancipated. Like Dhroo and Prahlaad, they merge in the Lord. ||1||Pause||
Whosoever meditates on Him, he is emancipated and merges in the Lord like Dhru and Prahlad. Pause.
Whoever chants reaches liberation, and like Dhru and Prahlad will merge into Hari. ||1|| Rahau ||

CW35: Har jeeo = O Prabhu ji! Kar = showing. Naam = in the Name. Lagavaigo = joins.
O Prabhu ji! Show mercy, show mercy, show mercy (and keep me joined to Your Name. Parmatma Himself,) in His grace, joins (a being to His) Name.
Mercy, mercy, mercy - O Dear Lord, please shower Your Mercy on me, and attach me to Your Name.
O Sire Lord, show You, mercy, and kindness to me and mercifully attach You me to Your name.
Hari ji, the form and treasure of mercy, who shows mercy to you, will in His mercy attach you to His worship.
0WTZ: O Prabhu ji! In Your grace, unite (me) with the Guru. Only by meeting the Guru can (a being) remember (Your) Name. ||1||
Please be Merciful, and lead me to meet the True Guru; meeting the True Guru, I meditate on the Naam, the Name of the Lord. ||1||
Mercifully lead me on to the True Guru, by meeting with the True Guru, I shall dwell upon Your Name, O my Master.
O Hari! The one whom You, in grace, unite with the True Guru — that person, meeting the True Guru, will meditate on the Name. ||1||
2JBX: The dirt of ego from countless births sticks (to a being); joining the holy company, this dirt is washed off.
The filth of egotism from countless incarnations sticks to me; joining the Sangat, the Holy Congregation, this filth is washed away.
The filth of ego of many births sticks to me and it is by meeting with the saints society that this filth can be washed off.
The dirt of ego and possessiveness that has clung for many births will all be washed off by joining the company.
1534: Kaasat = wood, timber, a boat. Lag sabad = attached to the Word. ||2||
Just as iron, attached to (a boat of) wood, crosses (the river), so, joined to the Guru's Word, (a person) meets Parmatma. ||2||
As iron is carried across if it is attached to wood, one who is attached to the Word of the Guru's Shabad finds the Lord. ||2||
As iron, attached with wood ferries across, so does the man, attuned to the Guru's word, obtain the Lord.
Just as iron crosses by clinging to wood, so the one who finds Hari through the Guru's Word will cross. ||2||
TVKZ: Har ras = the bliss of Hari's Name.
Sit together in the company of the saints, the holy company; joining the holy company, the bliss of Parmatma's Name begins to come.
Joining the Society of the Saints, joining the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation, you shall come to receive the Sublime Essence of the Lord.
Join you the saints society, company of the divine oriented, for, meeting with the saints society, you shall be blessed with the Lord's Name elixir.
So, O people of the company! Join the true company of the saints, because whoever joins the company will come to taste Hari's nectar.
PKJ2: Karam = (deeds other than the Name). Kadh = drawing out. ||3||
But the proud person, kept away from the holy company, does (other) deeds; (such a person is) drawing water out (of their vessel) and filling (it) with mud. ||3||
But not joining the Sangat, and committing actions in egotistical pride, is like drawing out clean water, and throwing it in the mud. ||3||
Whosoever associates not with the saints and does deeds of ego, he is like a person, who draws out water and throws it in mud.
The person who, without the company, does deeds in pride will pour the mud of ego, or desire, into the water of good deeds. ||3||
0B1K: Prabhu ji Himself stays the protector of His devotees; (that is why) the nectar of Hari's Name feels sweet to the devotees.
The Lord is the Protector and Saving Grace of His humble devotees. The Lord's Sublime Essence seems so sweet to these humble beings.
God is the Protector of the saintly persons and God's name elixir tastes sweet to the saints.
The servants to whom the Guru makes Hari's nectar sweet — Hari is the protector of those devotees.
0LKD: Khin khin = every instant, at every moment. Dei = gives. Updes = in the teaching. ||4||
Prabhu gives (His devotees His) Name (to chant) at every instant, and gives (the Name's) glory. The devotee stays merged in the Guru's teaching (Word). ||4||
Each and every instant, they are blessed with the Glorious Greatness of the Naam; through the Teachings of the True Guru, they are absorbed in Him. ||4||
Them, the Lord blessed with glory every moment and, through the True Guru's instruction, they merge in Him.
The one to whom the True Guru gives the glory of the Name at every instant — that devotee will merge into Parmeshvar through the True Guru's teaching. ||4||
5X8B: Kau = before, to. Niv = bowing. Raheeai = one should stay. Jan nivah = the devotees bow. Ta = then. Phal gun = the fruit of spiritual virtues. Pavaigo = gains.
One should always bow one's head before Prabhu's devotees; the devotees (themselves) live in humility. (When a person bows,) then (alone) they gain the fruit of spiritual virtues.
Bow forever in deep respect to the humble devotees; if you bow to those humble beings, you shall obtain the fruit of virtue.
Ever pay you obeisance to the Lord's devotees. if you bow to the God's slaves, you shall obtain the fruit of virtues.
Stay always bowed before the devotees. If you bow before the devotees, you will gain the fruit that is virtues.
70VD: Karah = do. Jiu = like. Pach javaigo = is ruined. ||5||
The wicked people who slander the devotees (are ruined themselves. The slanderer is always) ruined like Harnakhas. ||5||
Those wicked enemies who slander the devotees are destroyed, like Harnaakhash. ||5||
the villains, who slander the saints are wasted away like Harnakhsh.
The wicked one who slanders the devotees will burn up like Harnakhas. It is not caste that is worshipped but austerity. ||5|| ☬ He shows this:
NX4A: Brahm = Brahma. Kamal put = son of the lotus (Brahma is held to have been born from the navel-lotus). Meen = fish (Vyas is held to be the son of Machhodari). Poojah = honour, revere.

Brahma is held to have been born from the navel-lotus; Vyas is said to be the son of a fish (Machhodari) (yet, though held to be born of such lowly places), through the austerity (of devotion to Parmatma) (both Brahma and Vyas) are worshipped (in the world).
Brahma, the son of the lotus, and Vyaas, the son of the fish, practiced austere penance and were worshipped.
Brahma, the son of Lotus and Vyas, the son of Fish, practised austerities and were worshipped.

Brahma ji is the son of the lotus — that is, arose from the lotus — and Vyas Dev ji came from the fish family, meaning from Machhodari. By doing austerity they had themselves worshipped — meaning, through worship and austerity you too will become worthy of worship.
MUJC: Bharman bharam = the greatest wandering. Chukavaigo = ends. ||6||
Whoever becomes a devotee, honour them. (Honouring the devotees) takes away the greatest wandering. ||6||
Whoever is a devotee - worship and adore that person. Get rid of your doubts and superstitions. ||6||
Whosoever is the Lord's slave, adore him, ridding yourself of illusion and doubt.
O brother! Whoever is a devotee, worship them; Hari will end your wandering in doubt. ||6||
A842: Jaatan jaat = the highest of castes. Dekh = seeing. Mat bharmahu = do not be misled. Suk = Sukdev (a Brahmin by caste). Pageen = at the feet. Lag = falling.

Do not be misled (even) on seeing the highest caste (into thinking devotion is the right of high caste. See:) Sukdev (the Brahmin) is falling at the feet of (King) Janak and remembering the Name (learning the way of remembrance).
Do not be fooled by appearances of high and low social class. Suk Dayv bowed at the feet of Janak, and meditated.
Be you not misled seeing the high and low caste, Sukhdev, the Brahman, contemplated his Lord repairing to the feet of Janak, the Khashtri.

Do not be misled by seeing high and low — your own high caste and the Guru's low caste. So it was that Sukdev ji, a Brahmin, fell at the feet of King Janak, a Kshatriya, and meditated on Parmeshvar — when the king made Sukdev stand outside to test him.
SC1Q: Joothan jooth = the worst of leftovers. ||7||

(When he came to Janak to learn devotion, the langar was being served. Sukdev was kept standing outside. All the leftovers from the leaf-plates of the people eating in the langar) fell on (Sukdev's) head; (see, yet Sukdev, though a Brahmin,) did not let (his) mind waver for even an instant. ||7||
Even though Janak threw his left-overs and garbage on Suk Dayv's head, his mind did not waver, even for an instant. ||7||
The left-over of the leafy plates fell over his head, but his mind wavered not even a bit and trice.

Then the (joothan) leftovers of the kitchen fell on his head — that is, the leaf-plates were thrown out after the meal, and behind the screen of the wall no one had seen Sukdev ji. But that rishi's mind did not waver for an instant, not even a sesame seed's worth. If you likewise do not waver, you will reach liberation. ||7||
9VCB: Janak janak = many Janaks (of King Janak's line). Baithe = kept sitting. Singhasan = on the throne. Lai = taking. Dhoor = the dust of the feet. Lavaigo = applies.

On the throne where many Janaks came to sit (in their turn), (the devotee-king Janak of that same line, seated on it, even as king) is applying the dust of the feet of the nine rishis (devoted to worship to his forehead).
Janak sat upon his regal throne, and applied the dust of the nine sages to his forehead.
King Janak while sitting on his throne, took the dust of the feet of the nine sages and applied it to his forehead.

And see: King Janak sat on the throne of Janak — that is, the throne of the first Janak. That Janak's name was Nimi; he rose from the throne and applied to his face the dust of the nine sages, Piplayan and the others. ☬ So, O beloved! Pray like this too:
HNH4: Thakur = O Thakur! Mai = me, those like me. Karavaigo = makes. ||8||2||
O Thakur! Show mercy, show mercy on (Your) Nanak (unite me with some devotee of Yours who) would make me the servant of Your servants. ||8||2||
Please shower Nanak with your Mercy, O my Lord and Master; make him the slave of Your slaves. ||8||2||
O Lord, show You mercy, and compassion to Nanak and make him the slave of Yours slaves.
Sri Guru ji says: O Thakur, treasure of mercy! When, in mercy, You make me too the servant of Your servants through the Guru, then I will become so. ||8||2||
C26C: Ras = with delight, with bliss, with relish. Man gavaigo = (the one whose) mind sings.
(The person whose) mind, (taking) the Guru's teaching, begins to sing (Parmatma's) virtues with delight —
O mind, follow the Guru's Teachings, and joyfully sing God's Praises.
O my Soul, by the Guru's instruction, sing you, the praises of your God with love.
O my mind! If, taking the Guru's teaching, you sing Vahiguru's virtues with (ras) love, then you will be liberated.
ZTMG: Jihva = (their) tongue. Hoe = becoming. Koti = kot, millions. Dhiavaigo = chants. ||1|| Rahau ||
(so much love wakes in them that their) tongue, from one, becomes (as it were) hundreds of thousands and millions and begins to chant (the Name) (it never tires of chanting the Name). ||1|| Rahau ||
If my one tongue became hundreds of thousands and millions, I would meditate on Him millions and millions of times. ||1||Pause||
May my one tongue becomes lacs and millions; with these lacs and millions of tongues, I would sing the praises of my Lord a myriad times over. Pause.

So have such faith: O Prabhu! May my one tongue become hundreds of thousands, and hundreds of thousands millions. With those I will meditate on Your Name millions of times — that is, chant it. ||1|| Rahau ||
8AVS: Sahas phani = with a thousand hoods. Sekhnagai = by Sheshnag.
(Moved by that spiritual bliss) Sheshnag has chanted (Hari's Name always) with (his thousand) hoods. But, O brother, chanting Parmatma's Name, no one can find the end of Parmatma('s virtues).
The serpent king chants and meditates on the Lord with his thousands of heads, but even by these chants, he cannot find the Lord's limits.
The serpent King utters the Lord's Name with thousands of his hoods, but by so uttering he can find not the Lord's limit.

Sheshnag with his thousand hoods has chanted You. O Hari! Those who chant have not found Your end — meaning I too cannot find Your end; or: there is no end to those who chant — meaning very many are chanting.
0YXC: Agam = unreachable. Thahravaigo = stills, brings to rest, stops from wandering. ||1||
O Prabhu! You are a fathomless (ocean); You are forever unreachable. Through the Guru's teaching (the chanting person's) mind stops wandering. ||1||
You are Utterly Unfathomable, Inaccessible and Infinite. Through the Wisdom of the Guru's Teachings, the mind becomes steady and balanced. ||1||
You. O Lord, are exceedingly Unfathomable, Infinite and Inaccessible. It is through the wisdom imparted that the mind is balanced.

You are fathomless to the mind, supremely unreachable to the body, and unreachable to speech too. Whoever, taking the Guru's teaching, stills the mind in Your form — theirs alone will be stilled. ||1||
FVL2: Too = You. Neeke = good (of good life). Japtiahu kau = to those who chant.
O Prabhu! Those who have chanted You alone have become people (of good life). Hari gives (spiritual) bliss to those who chant the Name.
Those humble beings who meditate on You are noble and exalted. Meditating on the Lord, they are at peace.
They who ponder over You, O Lord, sublime are those persons. whosoever contemplates his God, is blessed with peace.
Those who have chanted You are the finest people. O Hari! They are the ones who chant You; You will bring them to happiness.
FG80: Dasi sut = son of a maidservant. Chhok chhohra = a lad. Ank = to the breast. Gal = to the neck. ||2||
(See:) Bidar, the son of a maidservant, was just a lad; (but through the blessing of chanting the Name) Krishna is holding him to his breast, holding him to his neck. ||2||
Bidur, the son of a slave-girl, was an untouchable, but Krishna hugged him close in His Embrace. ||2||
Krishan hugged to his heart and bosom Bidur, and untouchable lad, the son of a hand-maiden.

Bidar, the son of a maidservant, a (chhohra) boy — meaning a servant, (chhok) one whose touch pollutes, meaning a Shudra, the lowest of all — Krishna ji held him to his (ank) breast and neck — that is, made him worthy of honour. In the same way Krishna will hold you to his heart and neck. ||2||
1208: Te = from. Opat = arising. Kaasat = wood, timber. Ang = on (its own) body. Taravai = keeps afloat.
Wood arises from water; (to keep this bond, water keeps that) wood (on its breast and) keeps it afloat (does not let it sink).
Wood is produced from water, but by holding onto wood, one is saved from drowning.
The wood is produced from water, so, taking the side of wood, the water drowns it not.
See: wood has arisen from water, so, taking its (ang) side, the water keeps the wood afloat on itself.
U8GB: (In the same way) Parmatma Himself makes His servants of beautiful life; He keeps His age-old nature. ||3||
The Lord Himself embellishes and exalts His humble servants; He confirms His Innate Nature. ||3||
Of Himself, the Lord God embellishes His slaves and upholds His innate nature.

Just so, O Hari! You Yourself set Your servants right by giving them devotion, and You Yourself keep Your (birad) vow of loving Your devotees. As it says: "Whoever comes to His shelter, He holds to His neck — this is the Master's way." And He will keep it in future too. ||3||
BTYB: Ham = we beings. Loh = iron. Naav = boat. Taravaigo = carries across.

We beings are stones (heavy with sins), iron (heavy with vices); (but Prabhu, in His grace, keeping us) in the Guru's company carries us across (the world-ocean), (as) a boat (carries stones and iron across the river).
I am like a stone, or a piece of iron, heavy stone and iron; in the Boat of the Guru's Congregation, I am carried across,
I am like stone and iron, yea, like a heavy stone and iron but, embarking on the boat of the Guru's congregation I am ferried across.

So, O Bhagvan! We are stone upon stone — meaning full of sins — and iron upon iron — meaning utterly dull. O Parmeshar! You will give us the boat of the Guru's company and carry us across the world-ocean.
37E4: Man = in the mind. Bhavaigo = feels dear. ||4||
Just as (Kabir) the weaver crossed through the blessing of the holy company. Parmatma feels (always) dear in the mind of His saints. ||4||
like Kabeer the weaver, who was saved in the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation. He became pleasing to the minds of the humble Saints. ||4||
Just as Kabir, the weaver, was emancipated through the saints society and had become pleasing to the pious persons mind, so shall I be emancipated.
Just as Kabir the weaver crossed through the true company, and was pleasing to the minds of the saints. ||4||
676T: Khare kharoe = standing. Marag = on the road. Panth = on the way. Dhiavaigo = meditates.

(The person whose mind, taking the Guru's teaching, begins to sing Hari's virtues with delight) keeps chanting (Parmatma's Name at every moment) while standing, sitting, rising, (walking) on the road,
Standing up, sitting down, rising up and walking on the path, I meditate.
Standing, sitting, getting up and walking on the road and path, meditate I on my Lord.
So, O (khare) pure Parmeshar! (Kharoe) Standing, rising, sitting and walking on the road, they meditate on You through the path of devotion.
2LDE: Satgur bachan = (absorbed) in the Guru's words. Padhar = level road. Padhar mukat = the level road to liberation. Mukat = freedom from vices. Janavaigo = shows, tells. ||5||
(That person always stays absorbed) in the Guru's words; the Guru's teaching keeps showing (them) the straight road to freedom (from vices). ||5||
The True Guru is the Word, and the Word is the True Guru, who teaches the Path of Liberation. ||5||
The True Guru is the word and the word is the True Guru. The holy word shows the way to emancipation.
The True Guru is the form of the Word, and the Word is the form of the True Guru; and that Word, or the True Guru, shows the (padhar) road to liberation. ||5||
N09Q: Saasan = while there is breath. Saas saas = with every breath. Bal = (spiritual) strength. Nih saasan = even when not breathing, even on leaving the body.

(The person who comes to long for Hari's Name) keeps gaining (spiritual) strength with every breath while breath lasts (chanting the Name); even when breath is gone, they keep remembering Parmatma's Name.
By His Training, I find strength with each and every breath; now that I am trained and tamed, I meditate on the Naam, the Name of the Lord.
Through the Guru's chastisement, I have become powerful to contemplate fearlessly the Lord's Name with my every breath.

(Saasan) O Commander! May I gain this strength in every breath: that, meditating on Your Name, I may be free of doubt. Or: (saasan) Yama, the one who punishes, gains strength breath by breath; so show this grace, that meditating on the Name we may be free of punishment.
YPZ8: Parsadi = by the grace. Boojhai = (the fire) is put out. Tau = then. Naam = in the Name. ||6||
(When) by the Guru's grace (the fire of ego within them) is put out, then through the blessing of the Guru's teaching they stay merged in Hari's Name. ||6||
By Guru's Grace, egotism is extinguished, and then, through the Guru's Teachings, I merge in the Naam. ||6||
When by the Guru's grace, man's ego is stilled, then, merges he, in the Lord's Name, through the Guru's instruction.
If, by the Guru's grace, the fire of ego and possessiveness is put out, then through the Guru's teaching, O Named One, the being merges into You. ||6||

BK0S: Jeea ko = of (spiritual) life. Jeean ko = of all beings. Bhavaigo = feels good.

The Guru is the giver of spiritual life to all beings, but the Guru does not feel dear to the unfortunate person (they do not take the gift of spiritual life by taking the Guru's shelter; the time of life passes by).
The True Guru is the Giver of the life of the soul, but the unfortunate ones do not love Him.
The True Guru is the giver of the spiritual life, but, the unfortunate ones love him not.
The True Guru gives the gift of life to beings — meaning the True Guru gives teaching to anyone — but He does not please the unfortunate.
7ZE0: Haath = in the hand. Partapai = suffers. ||7||
This time does not come into the hand again; then (the person) suffers and wrings their hands. ||7||
This opportunity shall not come into their hands again; in the end, they will suffer in torment and regret. ||7||
This opportunity shall not come to hand again and in great distress one shall regret in the end.
This time of human birth will not come into the hand again; the being will burn and repent. ||7||
ZQG6: Ko = anyone. Bhal = good. Lorrai = wants. Dheh = falling down.
If anyone wants their own good, (they should) stay at the Guru's door, having lost their self-centredness.
If a good person seeks goodness for himself, he should bow low in humble surrender to the Guru.
If some good man seeks good for Himself, he should lie Prostrate before the Guru.
If any good person wants their own good, let them (dheh dheh) fall down before the Guru with mind and body — that is, stay humble.
ADK1: Thakur = O Thakur! Mai = me. Bhasam = the dust of the feet. ||8||3||
O my Thakur! Show mercy, show mercy on Nanak, (that) the dust of the Guru's feet may stay on my forehead. ||8||3||
Nanak prays: please show kindness and compassion to me, O my Lord and Master, that I may apply the dust of the True Guru to my forehead. ||8||3||
Says Nanak, O Lord, show You mercy and compassion to me, that I may anoint my forehead with the dust of the True Guru's feet.
Sri Guru ji says: O merciful Thakur! In grace, give me the dust of the True Guru's feet, that I may apply it to my body and purify it. ||8||3||
HAZ3: Rang = in the colour of love. Rata = dyed. Gavaigo = keeps singing.
(The person who, to dye their mind in the colour of Parmatma's love, soaks their mind) in the mordant of the Guru's teaching — (their) mind is dyed in the colour of Prabhu's love.
O mind, be attuned to His Love, and sing.
Imbued with God's love, my soul sings His praise.
O my mind! If, dyed in Hari's love, you sing His virtues —
FJKX: Bhai = (plural of 'bhau') all fears. Tras = fear, dread. Nirmal = free of dirt, pure. Laag = mordant (before dyeing, cloth is given a mordant, boiled in salt or soda). Lagavaigo = applies. ||1|| Rahau ||
(Dyed in this colour, that person always) keeps singing (Parmatma's virtues); all their (impure) fears and dreads become pure (reverence and respect). ||1|| Rahau ||
The Fear of God makes me fearless and immaculate; I am dyed in the color of the Guru's Teachings. ||1||Pause||
Through the Lord's fear and adopting the mordant of the Guru's instruction, I am rid of other fears and dreads and am rendered immaculate. Pause.

then the people whose dread — the fears that the messengers of death and the rest bring, and the dread of birth and the rest — has been removed, and whose mind has become pure: taking their teaching, the (laag) mordant will take on you — meaning the mordant of union with the true company will take hold. ||1|| Rahau ||
0PPK: Sad = always. Bairagi = detached, free of attachment to Maya. Nikat = near. Ghar = in the (heart-)home.
The person dyed in the colour of Parmatma's love stays free of attachment to Maya; Prabhu dwells (always) near (those dyed in the colour of love); He comes to settle in their (heart-)home.
Those who are attuned to the Lord's Love remain balanced and detached forever; they live near the Lord, who comes into their house.
He, who is imbued with the Lord's love, remains ever detached and abides near God; Yea, the Lord comes into his home.
The one dyed in Hari's love stays forever detached. Though Hari is near all, those detached ones will find Him in the home of the heart.
RAC6: Pank = the dust of the feet. Jeeva = I come alive, I gain spiritual life. Kar = showing. ||1||
If I get the dust of the feet of those (fortunate people), I gain spiritual life. (But this dust of the feet Prabhu) Himself, in His grace, gives. ||1||
If I am blessed with the dust of their feet, then I live. Granting His Grace, He Himself bestows it. ||1||
If I am blessed with the dust of their feet, then alone can I live, Showering His benediction, the Lord, of Himself blesses me with it.
If one gets the dust of their feet, then there is life; Hari Himself, in His grace, will give it to you. ||1||
DBLE: Dubidha = my-and-yours. Lobh = in greed. Man korai = on the unprepared mind. Rang = the colour of love.
The people caught in my-and-yours and in greed — on their unprepared mind the colour (of Prabhu's love) cannot take.
Mortal beings are attached to greed and duality. Their minds are unripe and unfit, and will not accept the Dye of His Love.
The mortals are attached to duality and avarice, Their uncultured mind takes not the Lord's colour.
Through duality, beings are caught in greed; so the colour of Parmeshar will not come onto their raw mind.
B169: Phir = again. Ultio = turns back (when the mind turns from greed and the rest). Janam = new birth. Bachni = through the words. Lavaigo = applies, dyes. ||2||

Then, when through the Guru's words (their mind) turns back (from my-and-yours, greed and the rest), (they receive a new spiritual) birth. (The person whom) the Guru, the Being, meets — He dyes (their mind) the colour (of Prabhu's love). ||2||
But their lives are transformed through the Word of the Guru's Teachings. Meeting with the Guru, the Primal Being, they are dyed in the color of His Love. ||2||
By the Guru's instruction, man's way of life is changed and meeting with the Omnipotent Guru, he is imbued with the Lord's love.
Through the Guru's teaching the birth is turned round again. When the Guru, the Being, is met, then He will attach your love to Hari. ||2||
XRNB: Phun = again, again and again. Dhavat = wander. Trai gunia = the mind caught in the three qualities.
All ten of a person's senses keep wandering again and again. The mind gripped by (Maya's) three qualities does not settle (in one place) even for a moment.
There are ten organs of sense and action; the ten wander unrestrained. Under the influence of the three dispositions, they are not stable, even for an instant.
There are ten organs and all the ten continue qualities, too, remains not stable even for a moment.

The ten senses, of the three qualities, run in all ten directions and do not stay still for an instant; or the mind of one lustful for Maya of the three qualities will not stay still for an instant. ☬ If you ask how the senses and mind come under control, he says:
KBZ8: Parchai = is pleased. Vasgat = under control. Mokh mukat = freedom from vices. So = that person. ||3||
When the Guru is pleased (with a person), their mind comes under control; that person gains freedom from vices. ||3||
Coming in contact with the True Guru, they are brought under control; then, salvation and liberation are attained. ||3||
Pleasing the True Guru man overpowers them and he them, attains deliverance and emancipation.
Through the True Guru's (parchai) teaching, their movements come under control, and that person alone, who controls the senses, will gain liberation. ||3||
362D: Oankar = in Oankar, in the all-pervading Prabhu. Sabh = the whole world. Ekas mah = in the One (Prabhu) alone.
The One Parmatma Himself pervades every place; the whole world merges into that one all-pervading One.
The One and Only Creator of the Universe is All-pervading everywhere. All shall once again merge into the One.
The One Lord alone is pervading all over and everything shall merge in the One Lord ultimately.
The One Vahiguru, the form of Oankar, is pervading; in the end the whole world will merge into that One.
A1ET: Ekas bachan = in His own one command. Bachan = in the command. ||4||
That Parmatma (sometimes) is one, Himself alone; He Himself (creating the world) becomes of countless colours. That Prabhu is leading the whole world in His one command. ||4||
His One Form has one, and many colors; He leads all according to His One Word. ||4||
The Lord of one from, has become manifest in many forms, and He drives all in His own command.
Vahiguru is the One alone, and He has become of many colours; all walk in His one word — that is, His command. ||4||
TYMC: Gurmukh = the one who stays facing the Guru. Lakhavaigo = understands.
The one who stays facing the Guru recognises the One Parmatma alone (dwelling everywhere). Facing the Guru, (a person) understands this secret.
The Gurmukh realizes the One and Only Lord; He is revealed to the Gurmukh.
The Guru-ward realises but One God and by the Guru's grace, he realises of One alone.
The Gurmukhs have recognised the One Parmeshar alone; so whoever becomes a Gurmukh and meets the Guru, the Guru will show Him to them.
18TK: Jai = going. Nij mahli = in one's own (true) dwelling. Anhad = (an-ahata, sounding unplayed) unbroken. Sabad bajavaigo = keeps the mighty influence of the Word (within). ||5||
The one who stays facing the Guru reaches Prabhu's feet; they keep the unbroken, mighty influence of the Guru's Word (within themselves). ||5||
The Gurmukh goes and meets the Lord in His Mansion deep within; the Unstruck Word of the Shabad vibrates there. ||5||
The pious person goes and meets the Lord in His mansion and then, for him, rings the celestial strain.
Those who speak the Guru's teaching without a break — those Gurmukhs have gone and reached their own true self. ||5||
EP41: Sabh sist = all creation. Gurmukh = the one who faces the Guru.
(In one sense) all beings and creatures (are made by Prabhu); (Prabhu) has created all creation; (but) the person who takes the Guru's shelter gains glory (in this world and the next).
God created all the beings and creatures of the universe; He blesses the Gurmukh with glory.
The Lord has created all the creatures and the world, but it is only through the Guru, that one is blessed with glory.
Of the creation of small and great beings that has been made, whoever becomes a Gurmukh will gain glory.
ADF4: Bin gur bhete = without meeting the Guru. Ko = anyone. Mahal = a place at Prabhu's feet. Aai jai = coming and going, in the round of birth and death. ||6||
Without meeting the Guru, no one can take a place at Prabhu's feet; (rather) they keep suffering in the round of birth and death. ||6||
Without meeting the Guru, no one obtains the Mansion of His Presence. They suffer the agony of coming and going in reincarnation. ||6||
Without meeting with the Guru, one attains not the Lord's presence and suffers pain in coming and going.
Without meeting the Guru, the true self is not reached. The being, being born and dying, will suffer on in this way. ||6|| ☬ Let them pray like this:
XGWK: Mere preetam = O my Beloved Prabhu! Kar = showing.
O my Beloved Prabhu! (Beings) stay separated (from Your feet) for countless births. The Guru (alone), in His grace, unites (them with You).
For countless lifetimes, I have been separated from my Beloved; in His Mercy, the Guru has united me with Him.
Since many births, I am separated from my Beloved Lord. Showing mercy, the Guru shall unite me with Him.
My Beloved Vahiguru, we beings have been separated from You for countless births. Those on whom You show grace, You unite with the Guru.
F7YY: Satgur milat = on meeting the Guru. Maleen = made dirty with vices. Bigsavaigo = makes blossom. ||7||
On meeting the Guru, (a person) gains great bliss. (The Guru) brings (a person's) intellect, dirtied (by vices), to blossom. ||7||
Meeting the True Guru, I have found absolute peace, and my polluted intellect blossoms forth. ||7||
Meeting with the True Guru, I have obtained supreme bliss and my soiled mind has blossomed.
Meeting the True Guru, they have found great peace; He makes their dirty understanding blossom. ||7||
ASHM: Jagjeevan = O Prabhu, the Life of the world! Mai sardha = my faith. Naam = in (Your) Name.
O Hari, Life of the world! Show mercy, (that the Guru) may keep my faith in (Your) Name.
O Lord, Har, Har, please grant Your Grace; O Life of the World, instill faith in the Naam within me.
O Lord, Master, the life of the world, show You mercy to me and instill faith in me in Your Name.
So, O Hari, Life of the world! When You show me grace in every way, O Named One, then my mind will fix itself in my faith.
1YFG: Mai = me. Saran = in Prabhu's shelter. ||8||4||
O Nanak! (To join Prabhu's feet) the Guru alone (is the means); the Guru alone (is the go-between). The Guru alone can keep me settled in Prabhu's shelter. ||8||4||
Nanak is the Guru, the Guru, the True Guru; I am immersed in the Sanctuary of the True Guru. ||8||4||
O Nanak, the Great God is the True Guru and in the refuge of the True Guru, I shall ever abide.

Sri Guru ji says: You are the (guru) great One; You are the form of the True Guru, and the True Guru is Your form. So, O Vahiguru, the True Guru will give me Your shelter and unite me with You. ||8||4||
SSYZ: Man = O mind! Gurmat = the Guru's teaching (alone). Chaal = the gait (of true life).
O mind! The Guru's teaching (alone) can make (you) walk the gait (of true life).
O mind, walk on the Path of the Guru's Teachings.
O my soul, walk you on the path, which is in accordance with the instruction of the Guru.
O mind! Through the Guru's teaching you will walk the good way — meaning your conduct will become excellent.
E1MX: Maigal = elephant. Deejai = is kept. Tal kunde = under the goad. Ankas = the goad (used to drive an elephant). Drirravaigo = makes firm in the heart. ||1|| Rahau ||
The Guru's Word is (as it were the) goad (with which an elephant is driven). As a wild elephant is kept under the goad, (so the Guru) makes (His) Word firm in (a person's) heart. ||1|| Rahau ||
Just as the wild elephant is subdued by the prod, the mind is disciplined by the Word of the Guru's Shabad. ||1||Pause||
As the wild elephant, subjected to an iron-goad, is subdued, so is the mind disciplined with the goad of the Guru's teaching. Pause.

Just as a (maigal) maddened elephant is put under the goad and comes under control, so, if the Guru gives the (sabad) teaching that is the goad, the elephant of the mind will come under the being's control. ||1|| Rahau ||
HMTK: Chaltau chalai chalai = wanders again and again. Dah dis = in the ten directions. Dis = direction. Rakhai = protects. Liv = longing. Lavaigo = brings about.
(A person's mind) keeps wandering in the ten directions again and again; the Guru saves (it) from wandering (and) brings forth love for Parmatma (within it).
The wandering mind wanders, roams and rambles in the ten directions; but the Guru holds it, and lovingly attunes it to the Lord.
The mercurial mind roams and rambles in ten, yea ten directions, but, disciplined by the Guru, it is attuned to the Lord.
In the world, which is a play, the mind, (dah) burning and restless, runs in all ten directions. When the Guru gives the Word and (rakhai) holds it back, then it will fix its attention on Hari.
5KQK: Dei = gives. Rid antar = in the heart. Mukh = in the mouth. Amrit = water that gives spiritual life. ||1||
The Guru settles (His) Word in (a person's) heart, and lets the water of the Name, which gives spiritual life, trickle into their mouth. ||1||
The True Guru implants the Word of the Shabad deep within the heart; the Ambrosial Naam, the Name of the Lord, trickles into the mouth. ||1||
The True Guru installs the holy word in the man's mind and the Name-Nectar trickles into this mouth.
When the True Guru lets the nectar of the Name trickle into the mouth, then He will give (sabad) Brahm to the heart — meaning make Him directly known. ||1||
7446: Bisiar = snakes. Bisoo = poison. Garurr = the Garur mantra.
Snakes are brimful of poison; (to save from their effect) there is the Garur mantra; (in the same way) the (person into whose) mouth the Guru puts (His) Word (-mantra) —
The snakes are filled with poisonous venom; the Word of the Guru's Shabad is the antidote - place it in your mouth.
Man is fully-filled with the serpent-like poison of sins but, the antidote of the Guru's word swallows them all.

The senses are (pooran) brimful of the poison of desire from the serpent Maya; or the snakes of lust and the rest are brimful of the poison of desire for women and the like. The Guru will put into the mouth His Word, the Garur mantra that takes away poison. ☬ Question: what will the mantra do? ☬ Answer:
WF96: Bhuiang = she-serpent. Bikh = poison. Jhar = charming away. ||2||
the serpent Maya does not come near them. (Through the blessing of the Guru's Word-mantra, He) charms away (their) poison again and again and brings forth longing for Parmatma (within them). ||2||
Maya, the serpent, does not even approach one who is rid of the poison, and lovingly attuned to the Lord. ||2||
The snake of mammon draws not near him who rid of the poison of sins and is attuned to the Lord.
The serpent that is Maya — or its work, lust and the rest — will not come near the one who, charming away the poison again and again through the Guru's Word, fixes their attention on Parmatma. ||2||
WPUJ: Suan = dog. Nagar = the city of the body. Sabla = (sa-bal) mighty. Maar = killing.
The dog of greed stays mighty in the city of (a person's) body, but the Guru kills (this dog) in an instant and drives it out (from within them).
The dog of greed is very powerful in the village of the body; the Guru strikes it and drives it out in an instant.
The dog of avarice is very powerful in the body abode, but the Guru smites and expels it in a moment.
The dog of greed, mighty in the city of the body — the Guru will have it driven out in an instant with the blow of the Word.
VEVL: Aan = bringing. Har nagri = in Hari's city, in the holy company. ||3||

(The Guru) has brought truth, contentment and dharma (these virtues) and placed them in the city of the holy company; (to escape the dog of greed a person) keeps singing Parmatma's virtues in the holy company. ||3||
Truth, contentment, righteousness and Dharma have settled there; in the village of the Lord, sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord. ||3||
The Guru enshrines truth, contentment and faith in the body abode and then man sings the Lord God's praises.
The one who has brought and kept these virtues — truth, contentment and dharma — in the body, or has put faith in them, will chant Hari's Name in that city and sing Hari's virtues. ||3||
